metadata.title: Hardening the Frontend
metadata.note: Mycroft patent intelligence progress video 10. Real session: hardened the React frontend with three distinct error messages (404 wrong format, 500 server crash, network failure), a real loading spinner with contextual hint for the classify path, disabled inputs during fetch to prevent double-submits, and changed classify default to false so the free path is the real default.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Aishwarya from the Mycroft team. This video covers two real improvements to last week's frontend: what happens when something goes wrong, and what happens while something is taking time.

output: What happens when something goes wrong,
and what happens while something is taking time.

beats.narration_text: A generic Failed to fetch error tells you nothing. Whether the backend isn't running, the publication number is wrong, or the server crashed — the original UI said the same thing every time.

Method: three real, different failures deserve three real, different messages. A 404 means the publication number format is wrong — the error now says so explicitly, with a real example. A 500 means the server itself crashed — the error now points at the API key as the likely cause. A network failure means the backend isn't reachable at all — the error now says to check if the server is running.

The classify path can take several real seconds — a BigQuery fetch plus a Claude API call. The original UI just disabled the button and said Reading. The real improvement: a visible spinner, a contextual hint explaining why it's slow when classify is on, and disabled inputs during the fetch so nothing can be resubmitted mid-flight.

Classify now defaults to off. The free path — structural claims reading plus citation lineage, no Claude API cost — is the sensible default. Classification is still one checkbox away, but opting in is now a real, deliberate choice rather than a silent default.

beats.role_note: real screen recording — success and error states live
beats.narration_text: This is the real UI, live. Type a real publication number — US-10822628-B2 — uncheck classify, and click Read Patent. The claims come back: seven total, two independent, five dependent. The lineage: twelve citations, one patent, eleven non-patent literature. Now type something invalid. The error is specific: patent not found, check the format, here is what it should look like. Not a generic failed to fetch. A real, actionable message.

shot.note: USER-PROVIDED real screen recording of the hardened UI showing a successful request followed by a real 404 error message.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick one real interaction in an app you've built and ask what happens in the three most likely failure modes — if all three give the same generic error, that's the real thing to fix first.

props.command: claude "audit this component's error handling — what does it actually show for a 404 vs a 500 vs a network failure, and are they genuinely different?"

beats.narration_text: Hardening the Frontend. Built with Claude, for Humanitarians AI.
